raw_case_text:
A 58-year-old male, a farmer by occupation presented with persistent watering and intermittent discharge for 1 year. He had had multiple consultations earlier and was treated with topical antibiotics. Ocular examination showed edema of the right lower eyelid localized to the medial aspect with a pouting punctum. Canalicular curettage revealed the presence of pus and concretions which were sent for microbiological evaluation. Gram's stain of the smear showed Gram-positive branching filamentous organisms and Gram-positive cocci in clusters.
Nonhemolytic nonpigmented small gray colonies [Figure 3] grew on blood agar. These were identified as Brucella melitensis. Staphylococcus epidermidis and Actinomycetes were also isolated from culture. The organisms were sensitive to chloramphenicol [Table 1].

subjective.chief_complaint: A 58-year-old male farmer presented with a 1-year history of persistent epiphora (watering) and intermittent purulent discharge from his right eye.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 58-year-old male farmer experienced persistent tearing and intermittent discharge from the right eye for 1 year that failed multiple prior outpatient courses of topical antibiotics.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for 1-year right eye epiphora, intermittent discharge, and medial lower eyelid swelling.

objective.physical_examination: Localized edema of the medial aspect of the right lower eyelid with a classic pouting lower lacrimal punctum; canalicular curettage expressed purulent exudate and sulfur-like canalicular concretions.
objective.advanced_workup: Microbiological evaluation of curetted right lacrimal canalicular pus and concretions: Gram stain showed Gram-positive branching filamentous organisms and Gram-positive cocci in clusters; blood agar culture grew small, nonhemolytic, nonpigmented gray colonies identified as Brucella melitensis alongside polymicrobial co-isolates of Actinomyces spp. and Staphylococcus epidermidis, all susceptible to chloramphenicol.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Culture of expressed lacrimal canalicular concretions and pus isolated Brucella melitensis co-infected with Actinomyces spp. and Staphylococcus epidermidis (all sensitive to chloramphenicol), confirming polymicrobial right lower lacrimal canaliculitis involving Brucella melitensis. Treated with thorough canalicular curettage and targeted chloramphenicol therapy.
